title: Staged escape hatch and tenant-aware safety chain
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a composable circuit-breaker subsystem that provides per-dependency / per-model / per-tenant trip profiles with staged degradation (soft escape hatch -> controlled shedding -> hard trip) and deterministic safe fallback plumbing. The design must preserve SLOs where possible, allow predictable multi-region failover semantics, and offer observability and tuning interfaces for SREs and tenant owners. Objectives: 1) define threshold synthesis rules (latency, error-rate, backlog, cost-per-token) and tie them to tenant tiers and model affinity; 2) implement multi-stage escape hatch with hysteresis and automated rollback; 3) provide deterministic fallback routing (local cache, model-variant stub, cross-region reroute) and explain quality tradeoffs; 4) ensure safe default policies for new tenants and a migration path for existing configs; 5) add test harness, simulation runner, and rollout/metrics dashboards.
comments: 2026-01-26 - Kickoff: alignment meeting with SRE, runtime, and product. Consensus to avoid a single global trip for heterogeneous workloads; we need per-entity state and a unified policy evaluator.

2026-01-29 - Design spike: evaluated 3 windowing approaches. Decided on a dual-window approach: short alpha window for fast detection (30s, streaming count) + longer smoothing window for hysteresis (5m EWMA). Rationale: balance detection latency vs false positives on spiky traffic.

2026-02-02 - Trade-off: chose percentile-based latency triggers (p95/p99) instead of mean to avoid masking tail latency from heavy tail requests. Error triggers are split into transient (5xx count) and persistent (healthy probe failures).

2026-02-03 - Fallback design: primary fallback order will be 1) local prefix/KV cache hit, 2) lightweight model-variant (quantized/short-context), 3) cross-region warm pool (same model), 4) synthetic/placeholder response with clear degrade metadata. Documented quality expectations for each path in the design doc.

2026-02-04 - Implementation note: policy evaluator lives in request-router layer and emits decisions (NO_ACTION / SOFT_DEGRADE / SHED / TRIP). The runtime must honor SOFT_DEGRADE by reducing batch size and forcing short context; SHED uses probabilistic admission for low-priority tenants.
2026-02-05 - PRD link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/STABILITY/Per-Entity+Safety+Chain+PRD (internal). Please review fallback quality matrix section before Feb 12.

2026-02-06 - Benchmarks: local simulations show soft-degrade reduces p99 latency by ~28% at 60% load while keeping model quality drop ~3% (measured on held eval prompts). Metrics attached in Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd1234/escape-hatch-simulations

2026-02-07 - Blocker: need a small API addition in routing service to carry "fallback_hint" token through to the downstream aggregator. Raised ENG-30846 to track change; blocked until design review is accepted.

2026-02-08 - Security review scheduled; gating on KMS integration for synthetic fallback content where tenant PII could be included. Security team suggested mandatory redaction step for synthetic placeholders.

2026-02-09 - Next steps: implement policy evaluator + metrics instrumention (week 1), add unit/simulation harness + chaos tests (week 2), internal canary in staging with two low-risk tenants (week 3), roll to high-traffic tenants behind feature flag (week 4).
TODO: Add end-to-end e2e script that replays real traffic traces and validates failover sequence is deterministic and annotated in traces.
acceptance_criteria: Policy evaluator config supports per-tenant, per-model, and per-dependency rule overrides
Dual-window detection (30s short, 5m EWMA) with configurable thresholds via Console
Soft-degrade path implemented and measurable in metrics (latency, quality, cost)
Probabilistic shedding works per-tenant with deterministic seeding for reproducible tests
Fallback routing order enforced and annotated in traces for debugging
Automated simulation harness validating no-regression for 99th percentile latency under baseline traffic
Runbook updated and SRE playbook verified in dry-run
implementation_notes: Store per-entity state in the existing fast metadata store; use a compact sliding counter to minimize memory pressure
Expose a small set of tunables in the Console: short_window_ms, long_window_ms, p95_threshold_ms, error_rate_threshold, shed_probability
Use traffic-weighted sampling for heavy tenants when collecting training data for threshold synthesis
Add a strict audit trail for all policy changes to support Private deployments and compliance audits
